Confidence Interval Calculator

Build a two-sided confidence interval for a population mean from a sample mean, sample standard deviation, sample size, and confidence level. It uses Student’s t critical value, which accounts for the extra uncertainty from estimating population spread. Interval = x̄ ± t* s/√n with n−1 degrees of freedom. The t critical value is numerically evaluated from the selected confidence level.

How to use this calculator

  1. Enter sample mean, sample standard deviation, sample size and the remaining inputs.
  2. Select Calculate to see the answer and its breakdown.
  3. Keep a scenario, change an input and compare the results.

Use consistent units and check the assumptions below before applying the result.

How confidence interval is calculated

Interval = x̄ ± t* s/√n with n−1 degrees of freedom. The t critical value is numerically evaluated from the selected confidence level. For mean 50, SD 10, n=25, a 95% interval is approximately 50 ± 4.13, or 45.87 to 54.13.

x̄ ± t* s/√n, with n−1 degrees of freedom.

Assumptions & useful context

The result depends on the values you enter and the method described above. Displayed numbers may be rounded; calculations use the unrounded values. Check that this model matches your situation before relying on it.

Frequently asked questions

Does 95% mean this particular interval has a 95% chance of containing the mean?

In repeated sampling, 95% of intervals constructed this way would contain the true mean under the assumptions.

What assumptions matter?

Independent observations and a reasonably suitable sampling distribution; small samples require particular care with skew and outliers.
